issue_context.title: Parcel 2: Install-Package installs incorrect packages
issue_context.body:
# 🐛 bug report

The module name passed to [`install`](https://github.com/parcel-bundler/parcel/blob/v2/packages/core/local-require/src/localRequire.js#L46) is the full module name instead of the bare identifier.

To give you an example, I noticed this because Parcel tried to run the following into my repo:

```
yarn add --json @parcel/transformer-posthtml/package.json -D
```

## 💁 Possible Solution

Some sanitisation should be done to:

- Ensure that it isn't an absolute or relative path
- Remove the nested file specifier from the request

Meaning that Parcel would only run `yarn add lodash`, not `yarn add lodash/get`.

review_comments: You have `~`, but no matching case in the test. I have never seen a `~` in a module, is that a special character to allow for `-`?
I'll add a test, but it's mainly to disallow Parcel from trying to install local packages
Ow there's already a test for it as part of `Return empty on invalid modules `
